clue.text: Yell 'Get away!' with first sight of enemy entering

blocks.note: scram is a curt order to go away
the opening letter of enemy

explanation.surface: Someone shouts at an intruder to clear off as soon as a foe comes into view.

clue.text: Beacon lit, newly set on fire, finally becomes this?

definitions.text: Beacon lit, newly set on fire, finally becomes this?

indicators.note: newly suggests made over afresh, so the letters are rearranged into a new order
finally points to the very end of the word beside it, keeping only its closing letter

blocks.note: the nine letters taken as written, to be rearranged
the closing letter of fire

explanation.surface: A signal fire on a hill, once ablaze, catches everyone's eye.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: a lit beacon is precisely something you cannot miss.
explanation.definitionFit: A blazing signal fire is meant to be easily seen, which is what being conspicuous or observable means.

clue.text: Big car pulling up short in French region

blocks.note: a limousine is a large luxurious car

explanation.surface: A large car brakes suddenly somewhere in the French countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Limousin is an historic region of central France, known for its cattle and porcelain from Limoges.

clue.text: Fellow one met at church in tight garment

the Roman numeral for one
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A man meets someone at church who is wearing a close-fitting outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: A bodice is the close-fitting upper part of a woman's dress, often laced.

clue.text: Time for a lot of deliveries?

definitions.text: Time for a lot of deliveries?

blocks.clueFragment: Time for a lot of deliveries?
blocks.note: surface reading: a busy season for couriers and the post office, such as Christmas
setter's reading: deliveries are births, so this is a period when many babies are born

explanation.walkthrough: Deliveries suggests parcels; in a maternity ward it means childbirth.
explanation.definitionFit: The term names a period of sharply raised birth rate, as after the Second World War.

clue.text: Female priest who takes charge of things?

a rector is a parish priest in the Church of England

explanation.surface: A woman cleric is asked who runs the parish affairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A director is the person in charge who manages and oversees an organisation or production.

clue.text: Good Parisian, one brave saint

the Roman numeral for one
to brave something is to face it

explanation.definitionFit: Saint Boniface was the eighth-century English missionary who became the apostle of the Germans.

clue.text: Ban a revolutionary fellow in Bahrain, maybe

blocks.note: to bar is to ban
taken as written

explanation.definitionFit: Bahrain is an Arab country, so a man there is likely an Arab; maybe marks it as an example.

clue.text: Animal heading off in a particular direction

blocks.note: a beast is an animal

explanation.definitionFit: East is one of the four cardinal compass points, a specific direction of travel.

clue.text: Ronnie maybe is a 23?

clue.text: They offer more than one way of looking at things

explanation.walkthrough: The surface sounds like a debate about viewpoints; it is about spectacles.
explanation.definitionFit: Bifocal spectacles have lenses split into two parts for distant and close sight, giving two ways to see.

clue.text: Support teachers assessing work? They finish after everyone else

teachers who grade work are markers

taken as written
cover is shelter or protection

clue.text: Sang going round hotel, becoming animated

blocks.note: less means not so much
Anne is a girl's name

clue.text: Pompous and dour, not funny

blocks.note: the seven letters taken as written, to be rearranged

clue.text: Something distressing about the female, the one who warns of death

clue.text: One traipsed around in torment

blocks.note: the eleven letters taken as written, to be rearranged

clue.text: Reportedly ’ated being on a train?

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said, so we go by how a word is spoken

blocks.note: hated is abhorred; the apostrophe shows the H dropped, as in a Cockney accent, giving a'orred

explanation.surface: A passenger is hated, perhaps for being on the train.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'ated shows a dropped H, so the synonym abhorred is also said without its H; in British speech, without the R sounds, it matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Aboard means on or in a vehicle such as a ship, plane or railway carriage.

clue.text: Like something citrus maybe, giving help when cold is caught

clue.text: Extras, perhaps, in theatrical sequences

explanation.walkthrough: Extras in a theatrical setting suggests non-speaking actors, but the first meaning is from cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Byes and wides in cricket count as scores, and a show plays for a continuous season of performances.
